text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key habit is using clear naming conventions. For example, choose names like "totalPrice" instead of "tp", so others can quickly see what a variable means. Another good practice is keeping functions small and focused on one task. When functions do too many things, they become hard to test and reuse. Finally, clean code should be easy to maintain. If you follow these simple rules, other developers can fix bugs and add new features much faster.
